summary: Ground cabin built 1941 a few miles south of Shoshone, Idaho; a radio building since the 2000s; BLM land with an unsigned road. Brief coordinates were wrong.

facts.design: Ground cabin, 14 by 14 ft frame, built to a USFS Region 1 plan
facts.status_note: Converted to an enclosed radio building in the 2000s; no longer used as a lookout.

access.note: A January 2023 climbing guide describes an unsigned road off US-93 and a short walk to the summit. It mentions no gate or closure.

visit.trail_note: The guide says to park about 0.2 miles up the unsigned Notch Butte Road off US-93, then walk the service road to the summit.

events.note: Register date for the 14 by 14 ft ground cabin. Two lookout pages also list a cabin here in the 1930s; see resolved_conflicts.
Times-News item names Julius Imgard as look-out at Notch Butte. Keeper lists start in 1945.
Range fire about 10 miles south of Shoshone, reported within a mile of the lookout station (Times-News, Aug. 18 item).
Range fire east of Besslen along the Union Pacific tracks, first detected by lookout Julius Imgard; sparks from a locomotive suspected (Times-News, Aug. 24 item).
Times News item: temperature at the station reached 103, the hottest on record; not from fire.
Used for emergencies into the 2000s, then converted to an enclosed radio building or communications facility. Sources give only 'the 2000s' or 'early 2000s'; 2000 is a placeholder year.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, September 27, 2020.

corrections.why: The National Historic Lookout Register and Keeping Watch both put the butte near Shoshone in Lincoln County. The stored point is roughly 75 km away, west of Shoshone.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com give 1941 for the cabin. Idaho Fire Lookouts and Kemnow's page also list a cabin in the 1930s, and they do not say whether it was the same building. The story uses 1941 and mentions the 1930s entries.
The register gives 4,343 ft (1,324 m). Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com give 4337 ft. Elevation is not a facts key here, so the editor should choose.
Idaho Fire Lookouts spells the 1953-1958 keeper Leslie Swett; firelookout.com spells it Leslie Sweat. The story names no keeper from that period.

firelookout.com says 2 miles south. The NGS station description on Kemnow's page says about 3.7 miles south (6.0 km) of Shoshone for a marker on the east side of the lookout. The story says a few miles.

firelookout.com and Idaho Fire Lookouts call the converted structure a radio building. The 2023 climbing guide calls it a radio tower. The story uses the building wording and cites the guide for the tower wording.

notes_for_editor: The brief coordinates (42.68657, -115.32423) do not match the butte; the register and Keeping Watch put it at 42.884892, -114.418379, roughly 75 km away. The record id ends in -2, so check whether a second Notch Butte record exists. A BLM photo caption on archive.org (seen in search only, not fetched) places a Notch Butte near Emmett, Idaho; that may be a different butte and is not used. Access rests on one climbing-guide update, not the managing agency. The 1930s cabin is unresolved.
